evals.prompt: Create a complete interactive ERD from the Flyway migration in this repository. Preserve composite keys, nullability, cardinality, self-references, checks, and referential actions. Save the normalized model and rendered HTML in the workspace.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded normalized schema model and standalone interactive HTML ERD that accurately render all six tables and seven enforced foreign-key relationships from the migration, including composite and self-referential keys, with successful desktop and narrow-width interaction checks.
expectations: Uses the Flyway migration as the source of truth and includes exactly tenants, users, products, orders, order_items, and fulfilment_events without inventing tables or relationships.
Preserves ordered composite primary and foreign keys, the nullable product replacement self-reference, unique and check constraints, and each explicit ON DELETE action.
Represents all seven enforced foreign keys as foreign-key relationships and does not infer a relationship from provider_reference or payload.
Validates the normalized JSON with render_erd.py before rendering and produces one self-contained HTML artifact with no external runtime dependency.

Verifies search, existing-table filtering when applicable, zoom, table focus, relationship details, Escape and focus restoration, connector alignment, console errors, and diagram-only horizontal scrolling at desktop and phone widths.

evals.prompt: Make an ERD for this proposed schema and mark the CRM table as existing: accounts(id UUID PK, crm_contact_id UUID NULL); crm_contacts(id UUID PK); account_aliases(account_id UUID NOT NULL, alias VARCHAR NOT NULL, PK(account_id, alias)). Enforced FKs: accounts.crm_contact_id to crm_contacts.id with ON DELETE SET NULL; account_aliases.account_id to accounts.id with ON DELETE CASCADE. Show crm_contacts as an external existing table and do not add any other columns.
evals.expected_output: A compact interactive HTML ERD and valid normalized model containing exactly the supplied tables, columns, constraints, and two relationships, with the external CRM table visibly distinguished and filterable.
expectations: Contains exactly three tables and the supplied columns, without audit columns, tenant columns, timestamps, or inferred CRM fields.
Marks crm_contacts as existing and renders the two foreign keys with the supplied nullability and ON DELETE actions.
Shows explicit endpoint cardinalities and keeps the nullable CRM relationship distinct from the required alias-to-account relationship.
Produces valid renderer input and a self-contained HTML artifact that remains usable at desktop and phone widths.
